findings: The Product handoff defines the C → E → A → B → D risk priority but deliberately leaves DQ-04's exact PR slices and selectors open. Current-run evidence therefore has no named vertical-slice seam separating the fastest credible C/E proof from the remaining 21-criterion, six-journey scope; carrying the whole scope as one delivery unit would put deferrable A/B/D expansion on the critical path (specs/r0005-restart/spec.md:39-40,195).

J1 and J6 require actual supported-host evidence and explicitly reject simulation as a substitute, while DQ-02 leaves the host/version and observation contract unresolved. Deferring this capability check until final integration risks invalidating substantial simulation-only work and extending delivery through avoidable rework (specs/r0005-restart/spec.md:74,79,193).

DQ-03 leaves current boundary versions and additive/breaking migrations unresolved, but the handoff does not yet price deferral. Without a recorded adapter/backfill, retirement, and revalidation cost, Design cannot distinguish a reversible ship-now compatibility seam from a one-way migration that becomes costlier after multiple producers and consumers adopt it (specs/r0005-restart/spec.md:81,185,194).
decisions: Name a thin first vertical slice around the highest-priority C/E behavior: current candidate binding, genuine pass-with-blocker rejection, one bounded authorized correction, and unchanged-failure stop through public production interfaces. Keep A/B/D expansion and the remaining journeys outside this first slice behind explicit entry conditions.

Treat real-host capability, identity, start/terminal observation, and collection as an early time-boxed evidence spike. If the supported host cannot supply them, stop with the named capability gap before accumulating further simulation-only implementation.

For each deferred boundary migration, record the trigger, compatibility adapter or backfill work, retirement and rollback condition, and revalidation cost. Prefer an additive dual-read or branch-by-abstraction seam when current-source verification shows it is available.

Plan may own final dependency order, but every bounded PR slice should deliver one independently useful production-boundary increment with its positive/severed proof and rollback, so later scope can be deferred without discarding earlier value.
